title: mem item
description: One indexed item, as every read verb reports it. `score` is present only on search hits; `body` only where the verb reads the file (show, handoff, questions --wait, finding list, search --kind).

audience.description: Question rows: who answers. `orchestrator` is a worker's question, settled by the session driving the run; null is a person's, which is what the hub shows.

task.description: Question rows asked by an orchestrated worker: `<plan>/<task>`, so the answer can be carried into the task's next attempt.

heading.description: Wiki section hits in `search --json` only: the section's heading as written, `top` for the text before the first `## ` heading.

snippet.description: Wiki section hits in `search --json` only: the section's line with the most query-term hits and the next line with text, newline-separated, each cut at 120 bytes; null when the page changed under the index.

bytes.description: Wiki section hits in `search --json` only: the section's size in bytes, heading line included.

answered.description: Question rows in `questions --json` only: whether an answer item exists. The JSON twin of the text listing's ✓/? column.

options.description: Question rows in `questions --json` only: the offered answers, empty when none were given.

recommend.description: Question rows in `questions --json` only: the answer the asker would pick, or null when none was given.

answer.description: Question rows in `questions --json` only: the answer's body, or null while the question waits.
